description: APPLICATION FOR THE ERECTION OF A SINGLE STOREY SIDE AND REAR EXTENSION AND INSTALLATION OF RAISED PLATFORM TO REAR FOLLOWING THE DEMOLITION OF EXISTING SIDE GARAGE
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed single storey side/rear extension, by reason of its combined siting, height and depth would result in a visually intrusive, overbearing and dominant form of development that would create a sense of enclosure and potential overshadowing to the detriment of the amenity of nearby occupants, in particular, no. 6 Johns Lane, Morden. The proposals would be contrary to, in particular, NPPF 2024 Chapters 4 and 12, London Plan 2021 policies D3 and D4, Merton Local Plan Policies D12.1, D12.3 and D12.4.

Reason : 2 - By reason of absence of details of boundary treatment, the proposed raised platform would result in increased overlooking and loss of privacy to the detriment of the amenity of adjoining neighbours in particular, no. 6 and no. 10 Johns Lane, Morden. The proposals would be contrary to, in particular, NPPF 2024 Chapters 4 and 12, London Plan 2021 policies D3 and D4, Merton Local Plan Policies D12.1, D12.3 and D12.4.

Reason : 3 - By reason of the removal of existing trees and in absence of satisfactory replacement trees and landscaping, the applicant has failed to demonstrate the proposal would conserve and enhance the natural environment on and off-site and thus will impact on the biodiversity in the Borough and visual amenity of the locality to the detriment of the host dwelling and locality. The proposal is therefore considered to be contrary to London Plan 2021 Policy G7 (Trees and Woodlands), D3, D4 and Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies D12.3, O15.1, O15.3 and O15.4.

Reason : 4 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did not engage in any pre-application discussions.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
